title: Emotional Intelligence
author: Daniel Goleman
core_idea: IQ alone doesn't explain who thrives: a separate set of skills (self-awareness, self-discipline, empathy) often matters more, and unlike IQ you can build them in adulthood.
bullets: Stop treating IQ as the whole story. Goleman's starting point is that high-IQ people often flounder while people with modest IQ do surprisingly well, so check which emotional skills are missing before blaming a lack of raw talent.
Start with self-awareness. Notice and name what you're feeling as it happens, because the other skills depend on it.
Practice self-discipline as emotional regulation: manage impulses and moods instead of acting on whatever you feel first.
Build empathy deliberately. Read what other people are feeling, since that drives how your relationships and your work go.
Treat all of this as trainable. Childhood shapes it, but it isn't fixed at birth, and working on it pays off in your health, relationships and work.

try_today: Set a 5-minute timer, write down what you're feeling right now in one or two specific words (like 'anxious about the deadline,' not just 'bad'), then note what triggered it.
